name: Blackbird Ventures
identity_check: Confirmed as Blackbird Ventures (blackbird.vc), which brands itself simply 'Blackbird' on its site; its pitch form sits on the blackbirdventures Typeform subdomain, and Baseten's and TechCrunch's round pages call it 'Blackbird Ventures'. It is the Australian and New Zealand venture firm founded in Sydney in 2012 by Niki Scevak and Rick Baker (Wikipedia; both are Partners on the team page), with offices in Surry Hills (Sydney), Cremorne (Melbourne) and Karangahape Road (Auckland), and people in Brisbane and Orange. It says it has backed 188 companies since 2012 (Canva, Airwallex, Halter, Gilmour Space and Baseten among them) and announced its sixth fund, A$1.05 billion, on 2026-08-25. The Blackbird Foundation (blackbird.foundation), linked from the site, is an affiliated foundation, not the investing entity. Not to be confused with other firms that also use the Blackbird name.

Invests across every type of technology from software to space, describing itself as backing founders rather than sectors or stages.

open_items: HQ city: the firm says it is 'based in Australia and New Zealand' and lists three offices (Sydney, Melbourne, Auckland) without naming a head office. Sydney is recorded because Wikipedia says the firm was founded in Sydney and the team page has a Sydney office manager; no fetched page explicitly calls Sydney the HQ.

Fund numbering (I-VI) is inferred from the vintage table (2013, 2015, 2018, 2020, 2022) and the 'sixth fund' wording for 2026. Each vintage holds two funds (core and follow-on, or early-stage and growth); the split between them, legal fund names and exact close dates were not found. Close dates are vintage years, except Fund VI (announcement date; the post says 'raised', not final close).

Fund VI split between the early-stage and growth funds is not stated. Fund VI LPs named by IT Brief: Future Fund, Hostplus, Aware Super, HESTA (existing) and Adams Street Partners, Morgan Stanley Investment Management, Schroders (new). The post says Blackbird has returned more than $2.25B in cash on just over $3B invested; the For Investors page gives a 32.24% net IRR as of 30 June 2026.
The ~NZ$60M 2020 New Zealand fund comes only from Wikipedia (database); not confirmed on a primary or press page, and it is unclear whether it is inside the 2020 vintage's $647M committed capital.
USD equivalents of Fund VI (search-result hints ranged from about US$680M to US$750M) were not on any fetched page; Technode, Business News Australia, Citybiz and Business Wire pages returned 403.
check_range currency AUD is inferred: the Get Investment page writes '$' without a code; the Fund VI post says all its figures are AUD.

stated_sectors not recorded: the firm says 'We invest in founders, not sectors or stages' and invests in 'every type of technology from software to space'. Recent notes cluster in AI apps and infrastructure, robotics tooling, space, quantum and health.

requires_us_entity = no is inferred, not stated: the requirement is a 'strong connection to Australia or New Zealand', location matters less, and the firm prefers the Australian Investment Council open-source documents. Several portfolio companies (Ivo, Baseten, Enhance Labs) appear to operate from the US, but no US-entity policy is stated.
Indian founders: not stated anywhere; the remit is founders with a strong connection to Australia or New Zealand.

application_url: the 'Pitch for investment' button goes to the Typeform; the same page also links an Airtable form to submit a 'vision' (https://airtable.com/shrbkSsoDs798Gav3). The page promises a reply within a week and says no warm intro is required.

Partners: the team page links only internal profiles and the company LinkedIn page, with no personal LinkedIn URLs and no sector focus, so focus_sectors are empty. Alex Apoifis (Partner, Chief Operating Officer) is an operating partner and is not listed; Robyn Denholm is a Board Member; Principals are James Palmer, Max Meyer and Silk Kadala. Co-founder roles of Niki Scevak and Rick Baker come from Wikipedia.

Rounds not recorded: Remedy Robotics (Blackbird's Oct 2025 post says it has invested since the 2020 Series A, but names no current round; DCVC's 2025-10-08 post says Remedy raised $35M in seed and Series A without naming Blackbird); Coherence Neuro (Nov 2025 post says Blackbird continues backing it; no stage or amount). Blog posts not fetched: Springboards, Wonder Studios, Wonder, NextWork (US$4.45M seed), Clove (US$2.75M pre-seed), 'Investing at Day 0 of Marloo'.
Currencies: Alloy's seed amount ($11.5M, Startup Daily) is recorded as AUD by inference; Nomad Atomics ($10M) and Aquila ($3M) amounts are written '$' with no currency, so currency is left null.

Valuations not recorded as post-money because the pages don't say post: Baseten 'raised $300M at a $5B valuation'; Heidi valuation $465 million (Heidi blog); Gilmour Space 'valued at over AUD$1 billion'.
Company HQs and founding years are left null where the round pages don't state them (Marloo, Adora, Baseten, Ivo, Enhance Labs, Halter, Lorikeet, Nomad Atomics, Aquila).

Alloy is described as both Alloy Technologies (Blackbird, 2025) and Alloy Robotics (Startup Daily, 2026); same usealloy.ai company. The Blackbird blog index lists posts without dates, and older posts load via script, so it was not enumerated in full.
